caption: All values are taken directly from the analysis output file; none is recomputed here, and no pre-existing estimate changed when the Fabiano sensitivity analysis was added. Comparative pools report odds ratios and proportion pools report percentages. The primary comparative estimate is model-dependent: the random-effects model down-weights the large Berthold cohort through the between-study variance, whereas the fixed-effect, Mantel-Haenszel, and Peto models all return about 0.97, and every estimate crosses an odds ratio of 1. All pools contain fewer than 10 studies, so funnel plots and Egger tests were underpowered and were not produced, and publication bias was handled qualitatively within GRADE. In both MA1 and the MA3 continuer proportion, the overlap-robustness row and the Berthold 2013 leave-one-out row carry identical values, because omitting Berthold performs both operations at once; they are listed separately because they test different assumptions. The prediction interval for MA2 and MA4 is unstable at k = 2 and is not reported as reliable. Estimates and I2 values are rounded as in the analysis output file. Event-level data are given in Table S3 and the primary forest plot is Figure 2.
abbreviations: Abbreviations: CI, confidence interval; GRADE, Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation; I2, percentage of variability across studies attributable to heterogeneity rather than chance; k, number of studies; MA1 to MA4, the pre-specified pooled analyses; OR, odds ratio; PJI, periprosthetic joint infection; PsA, psoriatic arthritis; REML, restricted maximum likelihood; UM.FS, unconditional model with fixed study effects.

footnotes.text: Berthold's Results narrative on p.497 reports 25 events in the discontinuation arm, whereas Berthold's abstract and the column sum of Berthold's Table 3 both give 28. The primary analysis uses 28 of 872; this row carries the 25 reading. See Table S3, footnote [a].

A single sentence in Fabiano's narrative states that the 87 continuation patients had no postoperative complications, whereas Fabiano's Table 2, p.S25, records 1 wound infection. The primary analysis uses 1 of 87; this row carries the 0 reading. Because one cell is then zero, a continuity correction was applied in which 0.5 was added to each of the four cells of the Fabiano row, and to that row only. The correction moves the pooled estimate further from the null than the primary estimate while the confidence interval still crosses 1, so it demonstrates additional fragility rather than a different conclusion. This sensitivity applies to the comparative pool only; the continuer proportion pool retains Fabiano at 1 of 87, so the 5.7% proportion and its George-excluded value of 5.2% are unaffected. See Table S3, footnote [c].

Fabiano's comparative data were pooled in the primary analysis while its reporting quality was appraised with the JBI case-series checklist, because it is published as a short supplement case-series report. This row shows the pooled estimate with Fabiano removed.

Exploratory. Only 2 studies contribute, the flare definitions differ between them, and Vasavada's exposure is aggregate immunosuppression, of which biologics were 31% of the held arm, in arthroscopy rather than arthroplasty. Nguyen cannot join this pool because no continued-arm flare count is reported.

George carries 59.1% of the weight in this pool and its numerator is hospitalized serious infection within 30 days rather than a surgical-site infection, so this row is reported alongside the primary estimate in the Results.
